```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 17
    n_vehicles = 6
    Q = 62  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[24, 32], [27, 86], [46, 82], [64, 30], [26, 58], [34, 71], [38, 90], [52, 30], [52, 60], [44, 76], [54, 64], [13, 90], [14, 31], [89, 14], [83, 42], [66, 90], [6, 92]]
    demands = [21, 5, 22, 13, 18, 13, 7, 11, 19, 11, 8, 22, 24, 16, 23, 11, 6]
    time_windows = [[0, 327], [53, 116], [37, 99], [41, 103], [27, 87], [34, 119], [25, 87], [48, 124], [27, 87], [34, 125], [42, 98], [16, 98], [60, 139], [64, 152], [58, 148], [34, 134], [48, 103], [75, 140]]
    service_times = [7, 10, 13, 14, 8, 6, 12, 8, 5, 7, 5, 10, 7, 5, 15, 13, 6]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Memo: Vehicle Routing and Scheduling with Customer Time Windows

Overview
We operate a fleet of identical delivery vehicles from a single central depot. For the current planning horizon, we must plan outbound routes that cover all assigned customer locations. Travel times are based on straight-line distances between the depot and customer coordinates and between customers, with the working assumption that one unit of distance equals one unit of travel time. All vehicles depart the depot at time 0, and each must return to the depot before the operation closes for the day as defined in the data.

Routing and Scheduling Challenge
Each vehicle will make a single trip: it leaves the depot at time 0, visits a sequence of customers, and returns to the depot before the depot’s latest allowable time. Every customer must be visited exactly once. The key planning decisions are:
- How many vehicles to deploy from the available fleet
- Which customers each deployed vehicle will serve
- In what order each vehicle will visit its assigned customers
- Planned arrival and departure times at each stop, ensuring all time-related constraints are respected

Service Rules and Constraints
- Time windows at customers: Each customer has an earliest and latest acceptable time for the start of delivery. A delivery must begin within that window. If a vehicle arrives earlier than the window opens, it waits on site until the window start.
- Service times: Each customer requires a defined unloading/service period. After service is completed, the vehicle departs immediately. If waiting was required, service begins at the time window opening and departure follows after the service duration.
- Capacity: Each vehicle has a limited carrying capacity. The total demand of all customers assigned to a vehicle’s route must not exceed this capacity at any point during the trip.
- Depot timing: All routes must begin at time 0 and finish with the vehicle back at the depot before the depot’s closing time specified in the data.
- Single trip per vehicle: No vehicle performs multiple tours; there are no mid-route returns for reload.

Cost Structure
The total cost of the plan combines two components:
- Distance-related travel cost, based on the total distance each vehicle travels
- A fixed deployment cost for each vehicle that is put into service
Using a vehicle triggers the fixed cost regardless of how many customers it serves, so the plan must balance route distances against the number of vehicles deployed.

Goal
Produce a feasible and efficient set of routes that:
- Visit every customer exactly once
- Respect all customer time windows and service times
- Keep vehicle loads within capacity at all times
- Start all vehicles at time 0 and return them to the depot before the end of the planning horizon
- Minimize the sum of total travel distance and vehicle deployment costs

Assumptions and Notes
- Travel time between any two locations equals the straight-line distance between their coordinates, and distance units equal time units.
- All vehicles are identical and interchangeable in capacity and performance.
- There are no intermediate replenishment stops, and no split deliveries to the same customer.
